title: Distinct Lipid Binding Dynamics and Sodium Ion Coordination in the TRAP Transporter HiSiaQM Revealed by Multiscale Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
authors: Quan, Senwei; Davies, James S; North, Rachel A; Hall, Kelsi R; Turk, Liam S; Newton-Vesty, Michael C; Dobson, Renwick C J; Allison, Jane R
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多尺度分子动力学模拟研究TRAP转运蛋白HiSiaQM的脂质结合动力学和钠离子配位机制，属于蛋白质结构相关的计算模拟研究，方法为物理模拟，对象和问题均聚焦于膜蛋白结构功能机制。
abstract: Tripartite ATP-independent periplasmic (TRAP) transporters are substrate-binding protein dependent secondary transporters that leverage ion gradients to facilitate substrate translocation across bacterial and archaeal membranes. Although the structure of HiSiaQM horizontal line a membrane-embedded TRAP subunit from the human pathogen Haemophilus influenzae  horizontal line has recently been determined, its transport mechanism is not fully understood. Given the likely importance of lipid interactions and ion coordination dynamics to the transport cycle, we applied multiscale molecular dynamics simulations to investigate these two complementary aspects of HiSiaQM function. Our simulations validated an experimentally identified lipid-binding site (BS1) and provided insight into its lipid-binding dynamics. BS1 is preferentially occupied by the anionic POPG, which is stabilized through persistent hydrogen bonds involving residues H100, R104, and R181. Additionally, our simulations revealed a novel, less stable lipid-binding site (BS2) that is selectively occupied by POPE. We suggest distinct lipid-binding behaviors for POPG and POPE, with POPG forming more persistent interactions at BS1 and POPE engaging more transiently at BS2; however, these remain to be tested experimentally. Analysis of sodium ion coordination at two known binding sites (Na1 and Na2) revealed contrasting dynamics: Na1 exhibited stable ion retention through backbone carbonyl coordination, while Na2 displayed lower stability due to involvement of the flexible side chain of T561. Geometric tunnel analysis identified possible sodium-exit pathways, supporting a working hypothesis that Na1 may act as a stable anchoring site and Na2 may function as a transient ion-exchange point during the transport cycle. Collectively, our findings provide mechanistic insights into how specific lipid interactions and sodium ion coordination could modulate HiSiaQM transporter function.
abstract_zh: 三组分ATP非依赖性周质（TRAP）转运蛋白是依赖底物结合蛋白的次级转运蛋白，利用离子梯度促进底物跨细菌和古菌膜转运。尽管人类病原体流感嗜血杆菌（Haemophilus influenzae）中膜嵌入的TRAP亚基HiSiaQM的结构最近已被解析，但其转运机制尚未完全阐明。鉴于脂质相互作用和离子配位动力学对转运循环可能具有重要意义，我们采用多尺度分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟来研究HiSiaQM功能的这两个互补方面。我们的模拟验证了一个实验鉴定的脂质结合位点（BS1），并提供了对其脂质结合动力学的见解。BS1优先被阴离子型POPG占据，该结合通过涉及残基H100、R104和R181的持久氢键得以稳定。此外，我们的模拟揭示了一个新的、稳定性较低的脂质结合位点（BS2），该位点被POPE选择性占据。我们提出POPG和POPE具有不同的脂质结合行为，其中POPG在BS1处形成更持久的相互作用，而POPE在BS2处更短暂地结合；然而，这些仍有待实验验证。对两个已知结合位点（Na1和Na2）处钠离子配位的分析揭示了对比鲜明的动力学：Na1通过主链羰基配位表现出稳定的离子保留，而Na2由于涉及T561柔性侧链而显示出较低的稳定性。几何隧道分析识别了可能的钠离子出口路径，支持了一个工作假说，即Na1可能在转运循环中充当稳定锚定位点，而Na2可能作为瞬时离子交换点。总体而言，我们的发现提供了关于特定脂质相互作用和钠离子配位如何调节HiSiaQM转运蛋白功能的机制性见解。
